extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: A dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airborne microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.publisher: Conservatoire national des arts et métiers, HESAM Université and French-German Research Institute of Saint-Louis (ISL)
extraction.citeAs: Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors, Julien Hauret et al., 2024
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A total of 200 participants contributed to the dataset, with 188 retained after post-processing to ensure high-quality data. The recording process consists of four steps performed consecutively for each participant: speech-clean (15 minutes of reading sentences from French Wikipedia), speechless-noisy (2 minutes 24 seconds of silence in noisy environment), speechless-clean (54 seconds of silence in complete silence), and speech-noisy (54 seconds of reading in noisy environment). Participants were equipped with six audio sensors simultaneously: a headset microphone, forehead accelerometer, in-ear soft foam microphone, in-ear rigid earpiece microphone, throat microphone, and temple vibration pickup.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text utilized for participant readings originates from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Audio recordings were obtained from sensors worn by participants during the broadcast of 3D spatialized ambient noise. A significant proportion of the noise excerpts were sourced from the Audio Set, with a particular focus on noise classes relevant to BCMs applications, such as those encountered in battlefield and industrial environments. In-house recordings of concerts and street events in 3rd and 5th order ambisonics were also rendered around the participants.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A series of three automatic filters were applied to remove utterances with obvious deficiencies. The filtering process comprises two main stages: extracting indicators for evaluating audio capture quality and using these indicators to derive filters. Indicators include: PER (Phoneme Error Rate) computed using Levenshtein distance, L50 silence and speech levels, and SNR. Three filters were employed: discarding audio samples where PER > 10%, verifying sensor functionality by examining SNR[i,j] > 1.5dB, and detecting sensitivity drift by checking that Lspeech_50[i,j] > Lsilence_50[i]. A 20 Hz high-pass filter is uniformly applied to each acquisition channel. Voice Activity Detection timestamps are extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, and in rare cases where adjusted timestamps exceed original audio boundaries, audio is trimmed by 15 ms on the affected side.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Textual data was filtered to produce a simplified dataset with a minimum number of textual and phonemic symbols and to minimize pronunciation uncertainty. Textual filters excluded most proper names, retaining only common first names, French town or region names, and country names. Utterances containing numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, or syntactic errors were removed. Common text normalization operations were applied, such as lowercasing text and removing punctuation except for apostrophes. Phonetic transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), which contains 33 phonemes in French, was generated using the text phonemizer of the CoML lab. A phase of manual phonetic transcription was necessary for unrecognized words.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: whisper-timestamped model (speech-to-text engine based on Whisper that applies dynamic time warping to cross-attention weights), CoML lab text phonemizer
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age, gender. Mean age for females: 25.9 years (median 22, range 19-59). Mean age for males: 31.4 years (median 27, range 18-82). Overall mean age: 28.55 years (median 25, range 18-82). The dataset includes 97 female and 91 male participants.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables overcoming current limitations of body conduction sensors for speech capture in noisy environments, with potential applications in military operations, industrial settings, access control, intelligence gathering, and battlefield forensics. The technology could strengthen security by adding an extra layer of authentication and aid in revealing emotional states and tracking life signals during critical events.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is only available in French, restricting research primarily to this language. The temple vibration pickup and throat microphone pose the greatest challenge for ASR in quiet conditions due to their limited bandwidth. Some in-ear microphones are affected by acoustic sealing issues for certain ear canal anatomies that do not fit the sensor properly. A 'one-size-fits-all' design is ideal in theory, but molded eartips would provide a better fit in practice, although this would require considerable additional manufacturing time for each participant. The assumption that speakers produce speech at the same loudness in both quiet and noisy environments may not hold due to the Lombard effect.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset can be used for speech enhancement (bandwidth extension), speech-to-phonemes recognition, speaker verification, speech recognition, and developing voice commands and monitoring vital signs including heart rate. The speech-noisy subset primarily serves testing purposes. The speechless-clean subset can be used for tasks such as heart rate tracking or analyzing noise properties of various sensors, and for generating synthetic datasets with realistic physiological and sensor-inherent noise.
